title: Beylik of Sinop
capsule: The Beylik of Sinop was a Turkic coastal principality on the Black Sea, established under the Candarids (also called Jandarids or İsfendiyarids) following the collapse of Ilkhanid authority in Anatolia in the early fourteenth century. Sinop, with one of the finest natural harbours on the Pontic coast, gave the beylik strategic maritime value; the dynasty initially controlled only the port city before expanding inland to Kastamonu. The Candarids were absorbed into the Ottoman Empire under Mehmed I around 1417–1418, though they were briefly restored under Timur's partition of Anatolia after 1402 before final Ottoman incorporation; the attestation end-date of 1333 likely captures an early phase before the Candarids consolidated their hold on both Sinop and Kastamonu.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's territorial footprint is only approximately attested; boundaries are inferred from Ottoman administrative records and Byzantine sources, with no surviving contemporary maps.
